title: Chloro-Count deep learning shows more bundle sheath chloroplasts in rice mutants
summary: Chloro-Count, a deep learning tool for counting chloroplasts, showed that loss of OsHAP3H function increases chloroplast occupancy in rice bundle sheath cells by 50%. In one field season Oshap3H mutants had more tillers and panicles than controls or gain-of-function mutants. The tool also showed that 2D quantification is compromised by chloroplast position. Deep learning here is a quantification tool and field data cover a single season. Preprint of 2024-06-28.
ai_technology: Chloro-Count, a deep learning tool quantifying chloroplasts in bundle sheath cells
organization: National Institute of Agricultural Botany; Nuclear Institute for Agriculture and Biology; University of Oxford

evidence.tested: Comparison of loss- and gain-of-function OsHAP3H lines with controls and one field season.
evidence.unknown: Yield effects across seasons and peer-reviewed status are not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning quantified chloroplast number and size, enabling the phenotype comparison.
